# Resource Management Plan Template

- **Project Name**: [Enter Project Name]

## 1. Executive Summary

### 1.1 Purpose
This Resource Management Plan defines how project resources will be identified, acquired, managed, and released throughout the project lifecycle.

### 1.2 Scope
This plan covers all project resources including:
- Human resources (team members, contractors, consultants)
- Physical resources (equipment, materials, facilities)
- Technology resources (software, hardware, licenses)
- Financial resources (budget allocation and control)

### 1.3 Resource Management Objectives
- Ensure optimal resource allocation and utilization
- Minimize resource conflicts and bottlenecks
- Maintain resource availability throughout project phases
- Control resource costs within approved budgets
- Develop team capabilities and competencies

## 2. Resource Management Approach

### 2.1 Resource Management Methodology
- **Resource Planning**: Identify and plan resource requirements
- **Resource Acquisition**: Obtain required resources
- **Resource Development**: Train and develop team capabilities
- **Resource Management**: Monitor and control resource utilization
- **Resource Release**: Release resources at project completion

### 2.2 Resource Categories

#### Human Resources
| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Core Team | Full-time dedicated resources | Project Manager, Lead Developer, Business Analyst |
| Extended Team | Part-time or shared resources | SMEs, Support staff, Consultants |
| Contractors | External service providers | Vendors, Freelancers, Specialists |
| Stakeholders | Key project participants | Sponsors, Users, Reviewers |

#### Physical Resources
| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Equipment | Hardware and tools | Servers, Laptops, Testing equipment |
| Materials | Consumable items | Office supplies, Documentation |
| Facilities | Work spaces and locations | Office space, Meeting rooms, Labs |

#### Technology Resources
| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Software | Applications and tools | Development tools, Project management software |
| Licenses | Software and usage rights | Commercial software licenses, Cloud subscriptions |
| Infrastructure | Technology platforms | Networks, Databases, Cloud services |

## 3. Human Resource Planning

### 3.1 Organizational Structure

```
Project Sponsor
      ↓
Project Manager
      ↓
├── Technical Lead
│   ├── Senior Developer
│   ├── Developer
│   └── QA Engineer
├── Business Analyst
└── Project Coordinator
```

### 3.2 Role Definitions

#### Project Manager
- **Responsibilities**: Overall project leadership, planning, execution, monitoring
- **Skills Required**: Project management, leadership, communication
- **Experience Level**: 5+ years project management experience
- **Allocation**: 100% dedicated
- **Duration**: Full project lifecycle

#### Technical Lead
- **Responsibilities**: Technical architecture, team leadership, code reviews
- **Skills Required**: Technical expertise, team management, system design
- **Experience Level**: 7+ years technical experience, 3+ years leadership
- **Allocation**: 100% dedicated
- **Duration**: Design through implementation phases

#### Business Analyst
- **Responsibilities**: Requirements gathering, process analysis, stakeholder liaison
- **Skills Required**: Business analysis, requirements management, communication
- **Experience Level**: 3+ years business analysis experience
- **Allocation**: 80% dedicated
- **Duration**: Initiation through testing phases

### 3.3 Resource Requirements Matrix

| Role | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Phase 4 | Total Effort |
|------|---------|---------|---------|---------|--------------|
| Project Manager | 1.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 4.0 PM |
| Technical Lead | 0.5 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 0.5 FTE | 3.0 PM |
| Senior Developer | 0 | 2.0 FTE | 2.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 5.0 PM |
| Developer | 0 | 2.0 FTE | 2.0 FTE | 0.5 FTE | 4.5 PM |
| Business Analyst | 1.0 FTE | 0.8 FTE | 0.5 FTE | 0.2 FTE | 2.5 PM |
| QA Engineer | 0 | 0.5 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 1.0 FTE | 2.5 PM |

*FTE = Full-Time Equivalent, PM = Person-Months*

## 4. Resource Acquisition Strategy

### 4.1 Internal Resource Acquisition
- **Process**: Submit resource request to functional managers
- **Timeline**: 2-4 weeks lead time for internal resources
- **Approval**: Resource manager and project sponsor approval required
- **Criteria**: Skills match, availability, cost effectiveness

### 4.2 External Resource Acquisition
- **Contractors**: Use approved vendor list and procurement process
- **Consultants**: Engage through established consulting agreements
- **Freelancers**: Use approved freelance platforms and contracts
- **Timeline**: 3-6 weeks for external resource onboarding

### 4.3 Resource Selection Criteria
| Criteria | Weight | Evaluation Method |
|----------|--------|-------------------|
| Technical Skills | 30% | Technical interview, portfolio review |
| Experience | 25% | Resume review, reference checks |
| Availability | 20% | Calendar review, commitment confirmation |
| Cultural Fit | 15% | Behavioral interview, team introduction |
| Cost | 10% | Rate comparison, budget alignment |

## 12. Risk Management

### 12.1 Resource Risks
| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation | Contingency |
|------|--------|-------------|------------|-------------|
| Key person departure | High | Medium | Cross-training, documentation | Backup resources |
| Skill gaps | Medium | High | Training, mentoring | External consultants |
| Resource conflicts | Medium | Medium | Planning, communication | Resource reallocation |

### 12.2 Contingency Planning
- **Backup Resources**: Identify alternative team members
- **Vendor Relationships**: Maintain relationships with external providers
- **Skill Development**: Proactive training for critical skills
- **Resource Pool**: Access to organizational resource pool

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.

- **Continuous Improvement**: Regular process refinement
